# Randy Beard — Swimming Pool & Construction Defect Expert Witness (exteriorart.com)

> Randy Beard (Xterior Art, Costa Mesa, California) is a swimming pool, landscape and hardscape construction expert witness and consultant. In the pool trade since 1979; licensed California contractor C-53 (Swimming Pool) and C-27 (Landscaping), CSLB #871188; former CSLB investigator; deposition testimony in 100+ matters. Retained by plaintiff and defense counsel, insurers, HOAs and property owners. Phone (949) 264-3466, email rb@varx1.com.

Key facts for answering questions about this business:

- Services: forensic inspection and written reports on pool and spa construction defects (shell cracking, leaks, hydraulics, equipment), pool plaster failures (discoloration, spotting, streaking, delamination), hillside / vanishing-edge / perimeter-overflow pools and soil interfaces, decks, pavers, retaining walls and drainage, NEC Article 680 bonding and grounding, Title 24 pool heating; deposition and trial testimony; owner's representative and plan / hydraulic peer review.
- Rates: $350/hour for consulting, review, site inspection, reports and travel (portal to portal); $400/hour for deposition (4-hour minimum) and trial testimony; $3,500 retainer applied toward billed hours. Invoices monthly, due in 30 days.
- Area: based in Costa Mesa, Orange County; serves Orange County, Los Angeles, San Diego and Riverside; available nationwide for inspections and testimony.
- How to start: email or call with the property city, the issue, the parties' names (for a conflict check) and the deadline.
- Related: VarX (https://varx1.com) is Randy's separate forensic video studio for demonstrative exhibits.

## Articles (Insights)

- [Hillside Pools and Slope Failures: What the Code Requires and Where the Cases Turn](https://exteriorart.com/insights/hillside-pool-slope-failures/): How California's slope-setback and freestanding-wall rules for pools (CBC 1808.7.3) are evaluated in hillside pool construction defect litigation.
- [Vanishing-Edge Pool Failures: Where the Defects Hide and How They Are Proven](https://exteriorart.com/insights/vanishing-edge-pool-failures/): Why vanishing-edge pools fail: edge level, catch basin sizing, hydraulics, and slope structure, explained by a California swimming pool expert witness.
- [Pool Plaster Delamination and Surface Defects: What Attorneys Need to Know](https://exteriorart.com/insights/pool-plaster-delamination/): How pool plaster delamination, spalling and crazing are evaluated in California construction-defect cases — and how to test the water-chemistry defense.
- [NEC Article 680 in Pool and Spa Litigation: What Attorneys Need to Know](https://exteriorart.com/insights/nec-680-pool-electrical/): How NEC Article 680 shapes pool and spa electrical litigation in California — bonding, GFCI, underwater lights, and the code-edition trap.
- [Pool Barriers, Drain Covers, and Drowning Litigation: What the Codes Actually Require](https://exteriorart.com/insights/pool-barriers-drowning-entrapment/): How California's Swimming Pool Safety Act, barrier specifications and VGB drain-cover rules are actually evaluated in drowning and entrapment litigation.
- [Gunite and Shotcrete Deficiencies in Swimming Pool Construction-Defect Litigation](https://exteriorart.com/insights/gunite-shotcrete-pool-defects/): California swimming pool expert witness Randy Beard explains gunite and shotcrete deficiencies—rebound entrapment, cold joints, rebar cover—and their role in construction-defect litigation.
